data_and_models: Receipt photographs, voice and typed Spanish queries, per-user purchase history and daily books in Firestore. Two model uses only, both non-arithmetic: natural-language parsing into a structured expression and receipt line transcription (gemini-3.5-flash). Every number is evaluated by mathjs in code. External data is SNIIM, the Mexican Ministry of Economy's market price system - 49 central markets, 222 products, no API - obtained by defensively parsing an ASP.NET HTML page with browser-like headers and pinning a real saved response as a regression test. Five scheduled Cloud Run Jobs run the agents, with retries and a logged history.
limits_admitted: no field interviews and no paying customer yet, stated as something no amount of code substitutes for
the model does no arithmetic at all, by design - it only parses language into an expression
simulated personas are hypotheses, not evidence, and are labelled that way everywhere they appear
a receipt whose rows do not sum to the printed total cannot be saved (the page also records a user left stuck with a disabled save button by exactly that rule)
the cold-start alert could not speak until a user had three purchases of the same product

one_line: A money copilot for cash commerce that leaves no paper trail, in the Spanish people actually speak: the model turns a sentence into an expression and code evaluates it, a receipt that does not balance cannot be saved, and five scheduled agents warn you before you buy.

sections.accomplishments: Five agents that have run unattended every day with nobody at a keyboard, the execution history described as a column of green checks. A system that refuses to save money it cannot verify, where 'every receipt-scanning app we reviewed stores whatever the OCR returns'. An accuracy agent that knows the difference between being wrong and being blind: on a day Gemini was overloaded, two of its twelve test cases got no answer and it reported 10/10 correct with 2 unanswered instead of raising a false alarm. Unit economics read off usageMetadata for real responses - $0.0087 per text question, $0.0218 per receipt - then checked against the billing report's output-token line. And an honest accuracy number: 'zero errors in 30 evaluated cases' published as '0 errors in 30 cases; 95% upper bound on the error rate is about 10%', explicitly because '100% accuracy' is what makes a technical judge stop believing everything else you wrote. Submitted to the Build with Gemini XPRIZE showcase; no placement is claimed on the page and none is recorded here.
sections.challenges: Four problems are told as diagnoses, two of them as wrong diagnoses. The cold start: the price alert could only compare a user's own history, so it needed three purchases of the same product before it could say anything, and in production that read avisos_creados=0 day after day - 'not a hypothesis, a measurement' - which is what forced the fifth agent and the SNIIM integration. A government endpoint answering 503 to anything without browser headers, for data that is public and free by mandate. The receipts-coming-back-truncated bug, where the team assumed the model was running out of output budget, added finishReason logging to confirm it, and the data said STOP rather than MAX_TOKENS: the model was stopping on its own, mid-word, deterministically at temperature 0. And two money bugs: Costco prints the weight on the line above the item, so the model copied the line amount into the unit price field and 2.845 kg at $433.64 became $1,233 for a row that reads $433.64 - the backend summed by line amount and said it balanced while the screen recomputed and said it did not, two sources of truth for the same number, leaving a user with a disabled save button and no way out; then a discount living in the totals block below the subtotal that the model kept forgetting. Even the Spanish gave them away: the first market alert said 'papa esta mas barato', wrong gender, fixed by putting an article on all 28 products and rewriting the message around a verb, which carries none.
sections.how_we_built_it: React 19 PWA on the front, Node.js and Express on Cloud Run serving API and PWA from the same origin, Firestore for data, Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash) for natural-language parsing and receipt transcription, mathjs for arithmetic. The central decision is stated as the one the whole product rests on: the model never does arithmetic - Gemini turns language into a structured expression and code evaluates it, because 'a language model is not a calculator, and money does not tolerate a plausible answer'. The agents are five Cloud Run Jobs triggered by Cloud Scheduler: no laptop open, no session running, retries on failure, every run logged. Wholesale prices come from SNIIM, the Mexican Ministry of Economy's market price system - 49 central markets, 222 products, no API - so the backend parses the HTML of an ASP.NET page defensively and tests against a real saved response 'so we find out the day the government changes the page'. Jest, 167 tests.
sections.inspiration: In Mexico most commerce is cash and leaves no record, so the food stall, the corner store keeping credit in a spiral notebook and the mother choosing between two bags of rice all do financial arithmetic in their heads or on paper while none of the software built for 'small business' was built for them. The reason they commit is a structural observation rather than a story: Brazil and Argentina have excellent public price-comparison systems fed by fiscal receipts, and the market vendor and the street seller are excluded from that data by construction - so as intelligence becomes cheap with AI there is an opening to serve exactly those actors. The framing is about who the data leaves out, not about what a model can now do.
sections.learned: Four lessons, each bought with a measurement. Instrument before you diagnose: both confident hypotheses about the receipt bug were wrong and both were fixed by adding a measurement rather than by reasoning harder. Thinking tokens are billed as output and dominate the bill - 417 tokens of thinking against 119 of visible answer, called 43% of the cost of every question - while the 2,596-token system prompt riding along on every call was in fact the biggest line. Simulated users are hypotheses, not evidence: a model generated six personas, which was genuinely useful for ordering what to go verify in the street, because agreement between personas reflects the generator's internal consistency rather than the world - and the page says it labels them that way everywhere they appear. And silence is a feature: an agent that speaks every day gets ignored within a week, so most days the correct output is nothing at all.
sections.what_it_does: Ask anything with numbers in it, in Spanish with typos and slang: 'cuanto es el 15% de 800 pesos', 'vendi 40 tacos a 25 y gaste 300 en carne, cuanto gane'. Photograph a receipt and every line is transcribed - discounts, coupons and per-weight items included - and the app refuses to save if the rows do not add up to the printed total. Ask which package is cheaper: 2 kg at $245 or 6.81 kg at $1,050, where the big one looks like the deal and is 26% more expensive per kilo. Five agents run on their own every day: one reads wholesale prices from the government's market system, one compares against your own purchase history, one closes the books at night. The alert arrives before the purchase, because 'an alert you read once you have already paid is worthless'. Voice and camera input on a mobile-first PWA.
sections.what_next: Receivables with a name: fiados, apartados, abonos and tandas as one data object - person, amount owed, partial payments, balance, age of the debt - which no app in the category treats as a category at all. Letting a user choose their central market, since the agent already takes the market as a parameter and a second city is one scheduler entry rather than new code. Extending to meat, grains and cooking oil, which SNIIM publishes in sections they have not parsed yet and which is what the taquero and the food-stall cook actually buy. Halving the cost by caching the system prompt and lowering the thinking budget for questions that need no reasoning. And field interviews plus a paying customer, of which the page says: 'We have neither yet, and no amount of code substitutes for either.'

testing: 167 Jest tests, named as including the invariants that matter: that a broken money JSON is never repaired by hand, that an agent never gives orders, that a receipt which does not balance cannot be saved. Separate from the unit suite, an accuracy agent scores twelve cases daily and distinguishes 'wrong' from 'no answer', so a Gemini overload day produced 10/10 with 2 unanswered rather than a false alarm. On the record's own evaluation of 30 cases the reported result is 0 errors with a 95% upper bound on the error rate of about 10%, and that bound reproduces exactly (1 - 0.05^(1/30) = 9.5%). Unit costs were read from usageMetadata and then cross-checked against the billing report's output-token line. No repository or CI link appears on the page, so the harness itself cannot be read; the figures it reports can.
